**5B.8 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Bottom line:** *Mixed, with a slight tilt toward partial redistribution rather than cleanly fair distribution.* Marcos did back some broadly shared gains and protective measures for farmers, poor households, disaster-affected areas, women, and Bangsamoro communities. But the year still shows persistent exclusion, red-tagging, underrepresentation of some groups, and signs that politically connected networks remained influential.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `SWS survey: PBBM very good on helping disaster victims, improving children’s education, helping the poor` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-09-14 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sws-survey-pbbm-very-good-on-helping-disaster-victims-improving-childrens-quality-of-education-helping-the-poor/) | The administration highlighted survey results showing strong performance on disaster response, education, and aid to the poor. This is the clearest broad-based positive signal for class distribution. | `5B.8`; also `5B.6` |
| `PBBM calls for comprehensive national flood-control plan to protect communities, production areas` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-26 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-calls-for-comprehensive-national-flood-control-plan-to-protect-communities-production-areas/) | Marcos responded to flooding by calling for a national flood-control plan and expert-led policy updates, which points to protection for vulnerable communities rather than narrow elite gains. | `5B.8`; also `5B.6` |
| `PBBM’s SONA: significant progress in BARMM, Marawi rehabilitation continues` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-24 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbms-sona-highlights-significant-progress-in-barmm-bangsamoro-leaders-react/) | The administration emphasized Marawi rehabilitation and progress in peace-agreement implementation, suggesting some regional inclusion for a historically marginalized area. | `5B.8`; also `5B.6` |
| `PBBM sees peaceful, orderly BARMM poll` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-06-24 | [link](https://mirror.pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-sees-peaceful-orderly-barmm-poll/) | Marcos publicly urged a peaceful, transparent first BARMM parliamentary election. This supports a limited regional inclusion reading, though it is still mostly rhetoric and election management. | `5B.8` |
| `Govt backs campaign to end violence against women` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-12-02 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-backs-campaign-to-end-violence-against-women/) | The administration backed a national anti-violence campaign framed around women’s rights and protection, which is positive evidence for gender-targeted distribution. | `5B.8` |
| `DSWD touts govt efforts to end violence, abuse against women, children` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-12-11 | [link](https://mirror.pco.gov.ph/news_releases/dswd-touts-govt-efforts-to-end-violence-abuse-against-women-children/) | Stronger referral, legal, medical, and shelter support for women and child survivors indicates concrete protection-oriented service delivery, though not full structural equality. | `5B.8` |
| `Marcos bans POGO, cites disorder it caused` | GMA News Online | 2024-07-22 | [link](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914272/marcos-announces-ban-on-all-pogo/story/) | Marcos framed the POGO ban as stopping torture, kidnapping, trafficking, and murder. This is evidence against privileging a politically connected, abusive sector over ordinary people. | `5B.8`; also `5B.5` |
| `Marcos orders total ban on POGOs` | Philippine Daily Inquirer | 2024-07-23 | [link](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964063/marcos-bans-pogo-cites-disorder-it-caused-ph) | The ban directly targeted a sector associated with criminal exploitation, which helped vulnerable workers and migrants rather than elite insiders. | `5B.8`; also `5B.5` |
| `U.S. Department of State report via ecoi.net` | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | [link](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html) | The report says the Marcos administration shifted drug policy toward treatment, due process, and rule-of-law investigations. That is relevant to poorer communities that bore the brunt of abuse. | `5B.8`; also `5B.5` |
| `Dangerous red-tagging of labor leaders in the Philippines` | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | [link](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders) | HRW says officials and security actors threatened union leaders and targeted women’s groups, Indigenous peoples, journalists, teachers, and judges through red-tagging. This is strong negative evidence against fair distribution across groups. | `5B.8`; also `5B.5` |
| `Red-tagging under Marcos puts activists at risk` | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | [link](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk) | HRW says officials and supporters accused critics of insurgent ties, putting leftist activists at serious risk. That undercuts the claim that gains were spread fairly across political groups. | `5B.8`; also `5B.5` |
| `Philippines report` | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House says women’s representation is concentrated in political families, Muslims and Indigenous groups are underrepresented, and no national SOGI/SOGIESC anti-discrimination law exists. It also says red-tagging persisted. This is broad negative evidence on group fairness. | `5B.8`; also `5B.5` |
| `Philippines report` | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | [link](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | The report notes a media JV tied to Prime Media Holdings and the Romualdez family, suggesting politically connected business networks still mattered under Marcos. This is indirect but relevant evidence against fully even-handed distribution. | `5B.8`; also `5B.5` |

**Synthesis**
- Best positive evidence: disaster relief, flood control, BARMM/Marawi attention, women’s protection, POGO shutdown, and due-process-oriented drug policy.
- Best negative evidence: red-tagging of labor and civic groups, underrepresentation of Muslims/Indigenous peoples, political-family concentration, and politically connected business/media networks.
- Overall, Marcos in 2024 looks more distributive than purely patronage-driven, but not cleanly fair across all regions and groups.

**Search gap**
- I found relatively little hard evidence on province-by-province budget incidence, class-disaggregated income gains, or measured regional redistribution. The strongest available record is about targeted vulnerable groups and institutional signals, not a full distributional audit.
